notes: Independent Round-2 verifier answers. Only reviews/blind/F.json consulted. Code-level correctness (shapes/masks/coalescing/reductions/GEMM/attention) verified independently.

answers.rationale: Both kernels are correct; (X) has heavy contention on out[0], serializing atomic-unit throughput. (Y) block-local tree + one atomic per block reduces to O(gridDim.x) atomics — same modulo FP32 non-associativity.
Naive three-kernel attention materializes S×S intermediate P (and S) in HBM: 2*S^2*2 bytes per (B,H). For S=8192, ~256 MB per (B,H) — quadratic and dominant.
num_warps/num_stages are per-Config launch params. Autotuner caches best config per key value and retunes on unseen keys. B false (retunes on new keys), C false (only user-provided list searched).

Write tile[tidy][tidx]: within a warp threadIdx.x varies with tidy fixed → stride-1 across banks. Read tile[tidx][tidy]: warp lanes vary tidx, addressing column ty — 32 lanes hit same bank → 32-way conflict; padding to [32][33] breaks column alignment.
__syncthreads() is block-wide; __syncwarp(mask) is per-warp. On Volta+ ITS, explicit __syncwarp is required around warp shuffle ops that used to be implicitly convergent.

C: standard warmup + sync + Event timing pattern. D: explicit rtol/atol appropriate for FP kernels. A false (Python time.time on async launches). B false (autotune/JIT/first-launch overhead should be excluded from steady-state).
tl.make_block_ptr builds structured pointer for [BM,BN] tile inside [M,N]; boundary_check=(0,1) tells tl.load to mask both axes; order=(1,0) makes axis 1 the fastest-varying = row-major.
CUDA Graph = captured DAG instantiated to cudaGraphExec_t, launched repeatedly with much lower per-launch CPU overhead. Especially valuable for short kernels.
Consecutive warp lanes read addresses stride*4=32 B apart; each 128 B L1/L2 sector delivers 4 useful bytes/lane → effective BW ~1/stride of peak (~1/8).
N is a runtime scalar arg reused across calls; BLOCK: tl.constexpr is compile-time — each distinct value triggers fresh JIT specialization with new PTX.
__constant__ is a 64 KB per-module region cached in a dedicated constant cache; warp-uniform reads broadcast in one access — best for lookup tables and per-block scalars.
FP16 has ~11 mantissa bits (rel ε ~9.77e-4); per-element rounding accumulates over K=4096. rtol ~1e-3 is a reasonable tolerance for FP16-in GEMM vs FP32-in reference — kernel likely correct.
cp.async issues async GMEM→SMEM copy bypassing registers; completion synchronized via cp.async.commit_group / wait_group (or mbarrier). Enables software-pipelined GEMM tile loads.

B: threadIdx.x<16 diverges within warp, serializes into two paths. C: blockIdx uniform across warp — no divergence. D: predicated ?: avoids divergence but may compute both branches. A false — compiler emits predication for suitable patterns.

A: correct via atomic_add over per-block partials. B: reduction order non-determinism → FP non-assoc → possible bitwise differences. C: mask+other=0.0 ensures tail lanes contribute 0. D false — atomic_add adds, not overwrites; initial value matters.
C: online-softmax recurrence over K/V tiles avoids materializing [S,S] in HBM; HBM traffic O(S). D: rescale factor exp(m_i - m_new) aligns previous acc anchor to new max — exact algebra. A/B false.

B: FP32 accum avoids FP16 precision loss over long K. C: on Ampere+, tl.dot(a,b, out_dtype=fp32) with FP16 lowers to mma.sync FP16-in / FP32-accum. A false (mma.sync natively supports mixed precision). D false (FP32→FP16 rounding is lossy).
Per iteration: load A tile 128*32*4 + B tile 32*128*4 = 32768 B; FLOPs = 128*128*32*2 = 1_048_576; AI ≈ 32 FLOPs/byte. A/C/D each misstate SMEM/register/BW dynamics.

GEMV per output: reads K FP32 from A + K from x for O(K) traffic, O(K) FLOPs → AI ~0.25 FLOPs/byte, well below A100 balance ~13. Kernel's stride-32 within warp on A is coalesced (lane k reads A[row*K + lane], addresses stride-1 across lanes).
Decode-phase attention: Q is 1 row; K,V of length S_kv must be fully read from HBM per step; low arithmetic intensity; per-step HBM traffic scales linearly with S_kv.
blockDim.x*y*z = 1024 = max threads/block; grid.y/z max = 65535; grid.x max = 2^31-1 on sm_60+ (so 65535 is well within). Launch is legal. A/B/D all invent nonexistent behaviour.
Fused single-pass keeps the row in registers/SMEM across mean and variance reductions; x is loaded from HBM only once. A naive two-pass re-reads x, doubling HBM traffic for large N/M.
mma.sync is warp-cooperative: all 32 lanes jointly execute one MMA, each holding operand/accumulator fragments in registers per hardware-defined layout. A single lane cannot execute an mma.
Register cap 65536/(96*256)=2.66→2 blocks; SMEM cap 164/32=5; thread cap 2048/256=8; block-count cap 32. Binding = registers → 2 blocks/SM = 512 threads = 25% occupancy.
Standard online-softmax merge: m = max(m_prev, m_new); s = s_prev*exp(m_prev-m) + s_new*exp(m_new-m). Rescales old sum to new anchor — exact algebra.
-inf is the identity for max; masked-off tail lanes filled with -inf never bias tl.max upward and never contribute a spurious max.

Persistent kernel launches fixed grid ~ SM count × blocks-per-SM and loops internally over work items from a global queue (via atomicAdd counter). Amortizes launch overhead and tail effects; trades away runtime scheduling.
Missing __syncthreads() between smem[tid]=x[tid] write and read of smem[tid-1] leaves a race: thread tid may read before thread tid-1 has written. Fix: insert __syncthreads() after the store.

log2(32)=5 shuffle-down steps: after loop, lane 0 holds the full warp sum; other lanes hold intermediate partial sums that don't equal the total. Consumers read from lane 0 or broadcast via __shfl_sync.
'Local memory' in CUDA is per-thread private storage backed by global memory (L1/L2/DRAM) — not on-chip; spills incur high-latency accesses. Heavy spilling typically kills perf.

BLOCK=N=4096 FP32 = ~16 KB registers/SMEM per program; each program handles one full row. This is a real occupancy constraint. A false (tl.sum uses register-resident tile whose masked lanes already carry 'other=0.0' from load, so extra mask on sum is not required for correctness here); C false (perf claim fabricated); D false (rsqrt isn't IEEE-strict).
Hillis-Steele: depth O(log N), work O(N log N). Blelloch: depth O(log N), work O(N) — work-efficient but more complex access pattern (up-sweep + down-sweep), often needs bank-conflict avoidance.
Subtracting row max is a mathematical identity (numerator & denominator both scale by e^{-x_max}); prevents overflow because FP32 exp overflows around x≈88.7.

C: same-stream ordering; different-stream concurrency subject to resources. D: event record + streamWaitEvent enables cross-stream deps without CPU block. A/B false — streams don't block each other by default; cudaEventRecord is async.
Progression: Volta FP16 (with FP16/FP32 accum), Turing added INT8/INT4, Ampere added BF16 / TF32 / FP64 Tensor Cores, Hopper added FP8 (E4M3/E5M2). Kernels must conditionalize on __CUDA_ARCH__.

Read-only path routes global loads through a separate cache optimized for read-only spatially-local data; triggered by __ldg or const T* __restrict__ on Kepler+. Improves L1 pressure for read-only inputs like weights.
pid_m=17, pid_n=3 with BM=32, BN=128 → rows 544..575, cols 384..511. Both within M=2048 and N=1024 → mask uniformly True.

For pid=976, tail lanes with offsets >= N (448 lanes) are masked in tl.load (using other=0.0) and in tl.store — no OOB access. A false (masked lanes don't emit real transactions); B false (no implicit bounds check); C false (mask affects both load and store).
Warp = 32 threads scheduled as one instruction issue unit (SIMT). Per-lane predication handles divergence within a warp.
nvcuda::wmma is a higher-level C++ template API (fragment types, load/store/mma) that lowers to mma.sync + ldmatrix PTX. Raw mma.sync gives finer control and is used by CUTLASS-class libraries.
